failure_summary.description: Agents answered a related entity or a truth value instead of the clue's requested referent, despite existing slot and wording guidance.
Clues involving adaptations or parodies did not reliably distinguish the source work or original character from the work presenting it.
Answers were either truncated by omitting an integral name word or made too specific by adding an unrequested subtype.

patch.reasoning: The skill already covers general answer-slot selection, so those failures do not warrant duplicating that guidance. These edits clarify the source-versus-adaptation/parody distinction and the difference between preserving integral name words and adding an unsupported subtype.

edits.target: When a question describes a title as changed, adapted, or parodied, distinguish the original title from the altered title. Use the wording to determine which is requested: a reference to the original work or an author's title asks for the original; a question asking what the adaptation, parody, or short was called asks for the altered title. Do not mistake the described change for the requested answer.
edits.content: When a clue concerns an adaptation, retelling, or parody, determine whether it asks for the source work or original character, or for the new work or title. If it asks what an adaptation or parody was called, give that altered title; if it asks what work or person it draws on or parodies, give the source work or original person—not the adaptation or the tale that features the parody. Use the clue's wording to identify the requested relation.

edits.target: For fill-in or clue-style prompts, supply only the missing headword or name component; do not repeat information already given in the clue or add clue modifiers unless they are part of the canonical answer.
edits.content: For fill-in or clue-style prompts, give the full conventional label at the requested level of specificity. Retain words integral to a name, such as a publication-type word when it belongs to the named title, but do not add an unsupported subtype or narrow a generic category just because context mentions one. For definition clues, choose the category that directly matches the definition, not a related role or narrower example. Do not repeat information already explicit in the clue; when asked to complete a supplied name, give only the missing component.
